An LLM Agent and Its ToolsAn LLM agent chooses its next tool or final answer from the goal and returned observations

The agent loop connects model choices with available external operations

ReAct: Reasoning and Acting

An action produces an observation that informs the next step

A ReAct Interaction

The example alternates a model decision with an external observation

Function CallingA model response can contain text or a named function request; the application executes it

The model can return a named function and structured arguments

A Function SchemaFunction body, callable name, then typed and required arguments

The schema describes the callable operation and its argument fields

Requesting a Function Call

A model request supplies messages and the available function definitions

The Returned Function Call

The response names a function and its JSON arguments; its text content is empty

Executing the Requested Function

The application parses arguments and executes the named function

Agent Loop and Stopping

The program repeats tool selection and observation until a stopping condition

A Fixed Chain

The developer specifies a fixed control flow around the model

Model-Selected Control Flow

The application can let the model choose its next path

Agent Control Flow

An agent gives the model responsibility for part of the control flow

Different Levels of Agent ControlFrom the Lecture 15 router chain to a model that chooses its own steps

Routing and autonomous behavior occupy different points on a control axis

Control and Application Reliability

Giving the model more control changes the reliability challenge

The Harness Around the ModelContext, tools, checks, budget and trace come from the program, not from the model

The model proposes; the harness decides what runs and what is kept

Tools Within an LLM ApplicationAgents and tools are one more LangChain component beside prompts, memory and retrieval

LangChain packages tools and the agent loop from part 01

LangChain Expression Language (LCEL)LCEL writes the Lecture 15 chain as prompt | model | parser

Composition connects a prompt, model and output parser

Tool Input Schemas

The tool schema communicates the argument structure to the model

The Observed Tool SelectionGiven a weather tool and a Wikipedia tool, the model names one per question

The returned call shows which operation and arguments the model selected

Building the Agent ExecutorThe executor is the part 01 loop: call the model, run the tool, repeat until finished

The executor connects tools, model requests and an intermediate message history

LangGraph MotivationLangGraph is a framework for stateful workflows and agents with explicit graph control

Explicit application structure can constrain the parts chosen by the model

Model Choice Within a Graph

The graph can combine fixed transitions with model-selected behavior

LangGraph Nodes and Edges

Nodes and edges express the application control flow

LangGraph and LangChain

Graph control and reusable application components play complementary roles

Nodes, Edges, and StateNodes update shared state; edges choose the next node using age and attempt count

The normal path gains a refresh branch and a bounded review exit

State UpdateA node returns the fields it changed

The Read node adds evidence to the existing task state

§ How Coding Changed

Software 1.0, 2.0 and 3.0Karpathy: programs as code, as learned weights, and now as prompts to an LLM

The prompt is a program; the LLM is the machine that runs it

Vibe Coding and Agentic EngineeringKarpathy (2026): the same agent, used with or without a spec, tests and review

The difference is not the model; it is who owns the spec and the review

The Autonomy SliderKarpathy (2025): the person chooses how much the agent does in one step

Move right only as far as you can still verify each step

The Generation-Verification LoopKarpathy (2025): the AI drafts, the person checks, and the loop should spin fast

A change too large to review is a change nobody verified

§ Loops

Case study: AutoResearchAn agent runs the ML experiment loop while the researcher sleeps

The agent takes the step a researcher used to take between training runs

ML Pipeline as an Agent LoopLecture 14 training and evaluation steps become the agent's tools and observations

A worse result discards the change and returns to the last kept version

What the Agent May ChangeThe human writes instructions; the agent edits one file; the evaluation stays fixed

A fixed evaluator keeps every experiment on the same scale

A Checkable GoalA loop can stop on its own only when a program can test the goal

The second goal names its check, so no reviewer is needed between steps

Loop EndingsThe program stops on completion, a limit, or a required decision

Reaching a limit leaves the task incomplete, not done

Caveat: Loops That Look BusyA running loop is not always a progressing loop

Each failure has a guard the program enforces, not a hope

§ Coding Agents

Spec Before CodeWrite what done means before the agent writes any code

Done when turns the request into a goal a program can check

Context Files: AGENTS.mdRules the agent needs every session live in a file in the repository

Short rules load always; long procedures load only when needed

Managing the Context WindowTool output fills the window fast; delegate, summarize and restart

What you leave out matters as much as what you put in

Review the DiffJudge the change and its tests, not the conversation that produced it

Merge only what you understand, however good the tests look

Permissions for a Coding AgentAllow safe actions, ask before risky ones, deny the rest

Ask first on anything you cannot undo

§ Graphs and Ops

When One Loop Is Not EnoughIndependent pieces and outputs consumed later call for separate nodes

Split the work, and each reader sees only its own piece

Graph EngineeringDesign multi-step agent work as nodes, edges and state, not one long loop

The same three parts as LangGraph, applied to a whole task

Isolation for Parallel WorkersParallel workers that edit files each get their own copy, such as a git worktree

Separate copies turn a silent overwrite into a reviewable merge

Structured OutputsRequire a schema, with a source field for every claim

A source field lets the next step check the claim instead of trusting it

Evidence-Based VerificationThe verifier checks each claim against its cited source and reports what it could not find

Not found is a valid result; a guess is not

Persistence Across SessionsWrite conclusions to files the next session reads, instead of relying on the transcript

The file carries the work across sessions; the transcript does not

Checkpoint and ResumeA checkpoint preserves progress across process restarts

Saved state does not make external effects exactly once; Lecture 17 adds request identity

LLMOps with LangSmithLLM operations (LLMOps) uses LangSmith to inspect traces and evaluate application behavior

The trace view connects the executed path with its recorded messages

Choosing the Level of ControlGive the model only the choices the program cannot make

Autonomy is earned by a cheap check, not by a better prompt

Takeaway: Agents

1An agent is a model that requests tool calls in a loop; the program runs and checks them
2LangChain wraps tools and the loop; LangGraph makes the control flow explicit as nodes and state
3Coding with agents: you own the spec and the review; loops need a cheap check, big work a graph
